First release of the maintained fork.

## Fixed

- A remote crash: a zero-length IAPrefix from a client holding a lease
  panicked the prefix plugin's matching pass
- A second remote crash on the DHCPv4 layer-2 reply path when no interface
  information is available
- Expired leases now return to the pool; on upstream the range plugin fills
  up forever (coredhcp/coredhcp#148)
- The prefix plugin recorded only the last lease when one request carried
  several hints
- The file plugin's v4 and v6 sections shared one record map, so the second
  clobbered the first
- Replies to relays honour the observed source port (RFC 8357)
- The generator's bare-name shortcut expanded to a wrong import path and had
  never worked

## Added

- Four plugins upstream does not have: options (any DHCP option from config,
  typed and validated), metrics (Prometheus text format, no dependencies),
  macfilter (allow/deny by MAC), ntp (option 42 and RFC 5908)
- Clean shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM
- ss-style `[ip6]%iface:port` listen specifications
- Nine fuzz targets, a benchmark suite, and a docker-compose end-to-end test
  with real DHCP clients

## Changed

- log/slog from the standard library replaces logrus, dropping nine
  dependencies
- The sqlite lease store uses the pure-Go driver: the whole server builds
  CGO_ENABLED=0 and cross-compiles without a C toolchain
- Every plugin keeps per-instance state instead of package globals
- 98.6% statement coverage, golangci-lint at zero issues on a strict config

## Container image

Multi-arch (linux/amd64, linux/arm64):

    docker run --rm ghcr.io/hyperized/coredhcp:0.1.0 -P
    docker run --rm --net host \
        -v /etc/coredhcp:/etc/coredhcp:ro \
        ghcr.io/hyperized/coredhcp:0.1.0

The entrypoint reads /etc/coredhcp/config.yaml; the server needs the host
network to share a broadcast domain with its clients.
